compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Blackwell sm_100, 82 SMs, 128KB smem/SM. FP16 tensor cores at 210/420 TFLOPS. Conv shape: N=1,Cin=16,Cout=32,H=720,W=1280,K=3x3,pad=1,stride=1. Output before pool: 1x32x720x1280. After 2x2 avgpool: 1x32x360x640. GEMM-equivalent: M=Hout*Wout=460800, N=Cout=32, K=Cin*Kh*Kw=144. Very skinny GEMM — N=32 is too small to fully utilize tensor cores (m16n8 wants N>=8 OK, but Cout=32 = 4 tiles only).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Compute = 2*32*16*9*720*1280 = ~8.5 GFLOPs. At 31.8 TFLOPS FP16 peak that's ~0.27ms compute-bound floor; bandwidth: input ~30MB + output ~15MB ~= 45MB / 896GB/s = ~50us BW floor. Likely memory/launch-overhead bound for this small workload.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Tensor core utilization limited by small Cout=32; may not beat well-tuned CUDA-core implementation.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input fp16: 1*16*720*1280*2 = 29.5 MB. Output fp16 (post-pool): 1*32*360*640*2 = 14.7 MB. Weights: 32*16*9*2 = 9KB (fits in smem/registers easily). Pre-pool intermediate (if materialized) = 59MB — should NOT materialize, fuse pool into conv.
memory_bandwidth.risk: If conv output materialized, doubles BW traffic. Must fuse.

register_pressure.notes: Weights (9KB) fit in shared memory comfortably. Per-thread: if a thread computes a 2x2 pool tile across all 32 Cout, it needs 32 fp32 accumulators (or fp16) = 32 regs. Manageable.
register_pressure.risk: Choosing too-large output tile per thread can spill.

nodes.notes: ANALYSIS: (1) Classification: fused stencil (3x3 conv) + elementwise (ReLU) + reduction (2x2 avgpool). Dense, contiguous NCHW fp16. (2) Math: out[n,co,oh,ow] = (1/4)*sum_{dy,dx in 0..1} relu(bias[co] + sum_{ci,ky,kx} w[co,ci,ky,kx]*x[n,ci,2*oh+dy+ky-1,2*ow+dx+kx-1]). Effective receptive field per output: 4x4 input patch across 16 channels. (3) Layout: x[1,16,720,1280] fp16 contig; w[32,16,3,3] fp16 (9KB - fits smem); out[1,32,360,640] fp16. Weights read-once-broadcast; input has 4x4 stencil reuse per pool output. (4) Regimes: small-batch (N=1) inference -> launch/BW bound; full conv compute ~8.5GFLOP, BW ~45MB -> arithmetic intensity ~190 FLOP/byte, looks compute-y but actual peak utilization limited by skinny N=32. (5) Knobs: tile shape in (OH,OW), Cout blocking (full 32 fits in regs), input halo staging in smem, vectorize via half2/uint4, tensor-core im2col vs CUDA-core direct, fuse pool inside same thread. (6) Skeleton: each block produces a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 8x32 pool outputs = 16x64 conv outputs = 18x66 input halo per channel). Load weights to smem once; loop ci streaming or hold all 16ci weights in smem (9KB). Compute conv into registers, apply ReLU, 2x2 sum, write fp16 output. (7) Families: F1=Direct fused conv+relu+pool with smem halo tiling (CUDA cores, half2 vec) — top pick, working set fits, single kernel, no global intermediate. F2=Tensor-core implicit-GEMM fused with epilogue ReLU+pool — N=32 limits TC efficiency; complex epilogue (pool reduces M). F3=Two-pass: conv+relu kernel then pool kernel — wastes 59MB of BW for intermediate, dominated. PICK F1.

action.description: Single fused CUDA kernel: each block produces a tile of pooled outputs (e.g., 8x16 pool outputs => 16x32 conv outputs). Stage input halo (16 channels x 18 x 34) into shared memory using half2 vectorized loads. Keep all 32 Cout weights (9KB) in shared memory loaded once. Each thread computes one or more pool outputs across all 32 Cout in registers (fp32 accumulators), applies ReLU, averages 2x2 conv outputs, writes fp16. No global intermediate. Use __ldg / cp.async if beneficial.
action.rationale: Avoids materializing 59MB intermediate, exploits 4x4 input reuse per pool output, weights tiny (9KB smem), arithmetic intensity high enough to hide BW.
action.title: Fused conv3x3+ReLU+avgpool2x2 with shared-memory halo tiling

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: CUDA cores fp16; 82 SMs need ~1800 pool-tiles for full occupancy if tile=8x16 (we have 360*640/128=1800 — perfect).
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Direct compute matches workload size well; avoids TC underutilization for Cout=32.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Inner loop scheduling may not hit peak FP16 throughput without careful unrolling.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Reads input once with halo overlap (~2x), writes pooled output once. ~60MB traffic ≈67us BW floor.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Halo overlap between blocks adds modest redundant reads.

register_pressure.notes: Per thread: 32 fp32 accumulators per pool output × outputs/thread. With 2 outputs/thread => 64 regs accumulators, plus working set. Should stay under 128.
register_pressure.risk: Spills if Cout accumulators × outputs/thread too high; may need to block Cout.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to n2 (tensor-core path) and n3 (two-kernel). Cannot combine — different memory/compute strategy. Primary candidate.

action.description: Block-Cout variant of fusion: each block handles a (pool-tile × Cout-subset) e.g., 16x16 pool outputs × 16 Cout, two blocks cover Cout=32. Reduces per-thread register pressure, increases occupancy. Compare vs n1 which holds all 32 Cout per thread.
action.rationale: If n1 spills due to 32-Cout accumulators, splitting Cout halves register usage and allows larger spatial tiles for better halo amortization.
action.title: Fused kernel with Cout-blocking (Cout=16 per block)

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: Each Cout block re-reads the same input halo => 2x input BW vs n1.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Lower register pressure may yield higher occupancy and better latency hiding.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Doubles input traffic — only wins if n1 is register-spill bound.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input read 2x (once per Cout block). +30MB ≈ +33us. Output unchanged.
memory_bandwidth.risk: BW cost may outweigh occupancy gain.

register_pressure.notes: 16 fp32 accumulators per output × outputs/thread; comfortable.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to n1 — uses Cout-splitting (different tiling strategy). Mutually exclusive with n1's full-Cout-per-thread design; can't combine since they define different block work assignments.

action.description: Implicit-GEMM formulation using WMMA/mma tensor cores: treat conv as GEMM of shape M=Hout*Wout, N=Cout=32, K=Cin*9=144 with on-the-fly im2col. Fuse ReLU and 2x2 avgpool into epilogue (reduce 4 spatial rows of GEMM output by averaging). Use m16n8k16 fp16 with fp16 accumulate for 420 TFLOPS path.
action.rationale: Tests whether tensor cores beat CUDA-core direct conv despite tiny N=32 (only 4 n-tiles).
action.title: Tensor-core implicit-GEMM fused with ReLU+avgpool epilogue

compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: N=32 only supports 4 n8 fragments; K=144 doesn't divide cleanly by 16 (needs padding). Pool fold-in across M complicates fragment->global mapping.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Tensor cores offer 6-13x theoretical FP16 throughput, but tiny N limits realized speed.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Epilogue pool requires cross-warp data movement or smem reduction; complex.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Same input/output traffic as n1; smem usage higher for GEMM tiles.

register_pressure.notes: Fragment registers manageable; epilogue staging in smem reduces reg pressure.
register_pressure.risk: Complex epilogue may inflate code size.

nodes.notes: SELF_CHECK: Alternative to n1/n2 — uses tensor cores instead of CUDA-core FMAs. Mutually exclusive with siblings because GEMM tiling structure differs fundamentally from direct stencil tiling.

kernel_summary: Fused Conv2d(3x3, pad=1) + ReLU + AvgPool2d(2x2) on fp16 tensors with shapes x[1,16,720,1280] -> y[1,32,360,640]. Compute ~8.5 GFLOP, BW ~45MB unfused (would be ~104MB with intermediate). Weights only 9KB so fit entirely in shared memory. Key constraints: must avoid materializing the 59MB conv-output intermediate; Cout=32 is too small for efficient tensor-core utilization so CUDA-core direct convolution with smem halo tiling is the leading strategy; fuse 2x2 average into accumulator so each thread sums 4 conv outputs before writing.
